dedupe_keys.name: digitaltransport4africa open gtfs and gis data for african paratransit networks

description: DigitalTransport4Africa (DT4A) is an open resource centre and digital commons for mapping public transport, especially semi-formal minibus services, across African cities. Its GitLab data group holds city repositories for more than twenty places, among them Lagos, Lusaka, Abidjan, Kinshasa, Kigali, Cairo, Alexandria, Nairobi, Maputo, Harare, Freetown, Douala, Bamako, Addis Ababa, Accra and Kampala. The Kampala repository, for example, contains GIS layers of routes, stops and terminals processed from field data, a GTFS feed built from the GIS and field timing data, transit maps and a codebook; it was collected in late 2019 and early 2020 for a French Development Agency study. Coverage is continental across these cities. The data are free and available to download from the GitLab repositories as GTFS, GIS files and PDF maps, with licences set per repository (the Kampala data carry CC BY 3.0). Caveats: each city was mapped once by a different project, so dates, methods and completeness vary, and semi-formal services change quickly. The feeds support accessibility, network flow and service planning models of paratransit systems, and studies such as minibus electrification. They follow the GTFS specification and complement the Kujala public transport networks for 25 cities.
